style: Original coarse pixel art inspired by Doom II-era software rendering

prompts.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: single style keyframe for a moving railway tunnel storyboard. Create ONE portrait 9:16 game frame in the deliberately crude low-resolution software-rendered aesthetic of 1994 Doom II: chunky nearest-neighbor pixelation, gritty indexed-color wall textures, flat sector-like light bands, strong distance darkness, coarse dithering, visibly jagged edges. Original environment and art, no copied game textures. Treat the frame as native 180x320 logical pixels enlarged by an integer factor: all bricks, rails, flames and objects obey ONE common coarse pixel scale. NO high resolution smooth illustration, no tiny polished details, no antialiasing, no bloom, no volumetric lighting, no depth of field. Subject: a soot-brown brick vaulted railway tunnel over glowing red-orange lava side channels. Three clearly separated tracks with wooden sleepers on masonry beds. Repeated heavy brick arch ribs, wall-mounted torches, low hanging black cables. Restrained dirty brown, grey, black and rusty red palette with small yellow-orange flames. Camera is in FRONT of and slightly above a small black steam locomotive looking back at its ROUND FRONT BOILER and two yellow lamps, cowcatcher toward bottom of image, train centered at 60% image height. Leave the lower quarter visible for tracks. Vanishing point at x50% y30%. Train remains fixed as the environment recedes behind it. Recognizable left-wall landmark at x12% y58%: iron torch bracket immediately above THREE pale bricks arranged diagonally. This landmark is for tracking motion in subsequent storyboard. Large overhead near arch, medium arch, far arch clearly separated by darker distance bands. Coarse dark pixel smoke behind train. Straight corridor, intact paths, no switches, no collapse, no interface, no text, no labels, no watermark. Emphasize authentic coarse old PC shooter raster and simple textured architecture rather than ornate modern pixel painting.

Use case: compositing and temporal storyboard. Using the supplied image as the STYLE AND SCENE MASTER, create a SIX-FRAME storyboard of this SAME tunnel moving during gameplay, arranged in a perfectly regular THREE COLUMNS by TWO ROWS grid with thin black gutters. Overall sheet nearly square but slightly taller than wide; each of six cells is portrait 9:16. Do NOT put six skinny strips side by side. No text or numbers inside the art. Maintain the exact coarse Doom II era indexed-color software-rendered aesthetic of the input: visibly large blocky pixels, grainy low-resolution brick textures, abrupt dark distance bands. Do not refine detail or smooth pixels. SAME front-facing locomotive held at EXACTLY same size and position in every frame, same three tracks, same fixed vanishing point and camera, no zoom or camera rotation. This is TEMPORAL MOTION of one straight corridor, not six architecture alternatives. Read frame order left to right top row then left to right bottom row. Simulate environment moving AWAY from the viewer behind the fixed train: foreground rails and sleepers slide UP toward horizon, the overhead arches shrink TOWARD the same vanishing point, near wall features shrink and move inward. Track the input's LEFT torch with three pale diagonal bricks beneath it across ALL SIX FRAMES. FRAME 1: matching input near large left torch and pale bricks near outer left edge. FRAME 2: that SAME torch and brick cluster has moved one quarter inward towards vanishing point, smaller; arch behind it contracts slightly. FRAME 3: marked torch now halfway to horizon, distinctly smaller, moving toward image center; a new near arch rib begins appearing at outer edges. FRAME 4: marked torch has receded beyond locomotive depth, tiny beside the middle-distance arch; next near torch enters from outside left edge. FRAME 5: marked original torch now very small near distant arch, new torch and new wall bay now occupy near left; near rail sleeper spacing has advanced visibly. FRAME 6: original marked torch almost lost in darkness near vanishing point, next wall bay occupies foreground with its torch and cables; establishes repeat rhythm. Foreground geometry must advance in perspective, not merely different flames. Train silhouette and headlights locked in place; tiny variations ONLY in flame shape, lava flicker and smoke behind train. Keep lower rails visible; no broken tracks, no branching, no changes of environment biome, no HUD, no cinematic blur. Clear practical art-direction storyboard.

Use case: temporal storyboard. Create a SQUARE 1536x1536 storyboard sheet, exactly 3 columns by 2 rows, six equal rectangular cells. Each cell 512x768, portrait 2:3. Thin black separating gutters only. Use supplied image as appearance reference for coarse 1994 Doom II style railway tunnel raster textures, but REMOVE THE TRAIN COMPLETELY from ALL frames. Background motion study ONLY, no locomotive, no smoke, no vehicle, no HUD. Large chunky pixel blocks, grainy indexed dark brown textures, abrupt lighting bands, zero smoothing. Fixed camera with SAME vanishing point at center x50%, y30% of each cell. Exactly three clear railway tracks in all six frames, lava side channels, heavy brick arches, cables. All panels show SAME corridor at six consecutive moments, ordered top-left to bottom-right. Key animation is one identifiable LEFT WALL TORCH above a patch of THREE LIGHT BRICKS. THIS SAME LANDMARK must move inward/upward and SHRINK progressively. Explicit panel-relative positions and sizes of this tracked torch: frame 1 center (12%,62%) large; frame 2 (23%,52%) size 80%; frame 3 (31%,44%) size 60%; frame 4 (37%,39%) size 42%; frame 5 (42%,35%) size 28%; frame 6 (45%,32%) size 16%. Keep the three-brick patch directly beneath the tracked torch at corresponding smaller sizes. Other repeating torch bays may enter at left border in later panels but WITHOUT pale brick patch so the tracked landmark stays unique. Every rail sleeper translates upward toward the horizon with perspective compression. One thick near arch recedes and SHRINKS toward the vanishing point across frames, a new large near arch enters around outer edges by frame 6. Arches never change construction, brick pattern translates with geometry. Ceiling crown approaches the horizon DOWNWARDS while the arch feet and rails approach it UPWARDS, all converge to same point. Lava flicker is secondary. Camera does NOT move sideways, tilt, rotate or zoom; depth motion only. Keep all three paths visible and intact. No environment destruction or new biome. Put tiny unambiguous white frame numerals '01','02','03','04','05','06' in black corner tabs at upper left of respective panels, no other text. This is a practical game background motion storyboard, not six random tunnel concepts. SQUARE full sheet, not tall 9:16 full sheet.
